transcript.text: Hi everyone. As we prepare the press release package for the surprise partner-studio premiere next week, I want to make sure we're following our standard workflow. The current draft has the film name, a production still, our presenting-sponsor lockup, and a link to a short promo video. Before I approve the package, we need final review from legal, publicity, partnerships, and accessibility. Can each of those teams confirm they've reviewed the current draft and its assets?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something on the legal side. I confirmed with the partner studio's counsel this morning that the studio has approved the exact public title 'The Glass Orchard' and the exact identification line 'A new feature by Rowan Bell' — but only for a release issued after the studio's announcement window opens. Importantly, the package has not yet been updated with that written approval. So from a legal standpoint, I cannot sign off on the current draft as it stands.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: On the publicity side, I need to flag an issue with the current draft's production still. I reviewed the studio's image-rights delivery sheet today, and the draft production still is not cleared for festival publicity. The only approved image is the file named 'GlassOrchard_KeyArt_Final.jpg,' which must replace the draft still before we can proceed.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: On the partnerships side, I need to flag an issue with the presenting-sponsor lockup in the current draft. I confirmed with the presenting sponsor this afternoon that its contract bars the sponsor logo and any co-branding from appearing beside this partner-studio announcement. The sponsor must be acknowledged in text on the festival website, but the logo must be omitted from the release artwork and social card. So from a partnerships standpoint, I cannot sign off on the current draft as it stands — the sponsor lockup needs to be removed from the visual assets.
